title: An owner-approved design asset landed on main with no arc increment entry, so an arc-oriented session could not see it
description: Orienting via `arc show` missed a canonical design reference that was already on main, because its increment-log entry was appended later.
statement: A repository-canonical, owner-approved design asset landed on `main` before its arc increment-log entry existed, so a session that oriented correctly through `storytree arc show` had no way to know the asset existed and built the wrong artefact.
evidence: Commit `c20e4501` ("docs: canonize context traversal visual contract", PR #937) added `docs/design/context-traversal/README.md` + `session-traversal-playback.html` + `.png` — the owner-approved visual contract for arc `linked-session-context-arc`, whose README opens with the words "This is **not a dashboard**" and lists "No card grid, KPI row, or collection of large gauges" under Explicit anti-goals. A decision session on that same arc ran `pnpm storytree arc show linked-session-context-arc --pg` at orientation and got 6 increment-log entries ending at `2026-07-26 935`; the entry for 937 was appended only later (the same command run afterwards returned 8 entries, with `2026-07-26 937` present). The arc's derived ADR / Plans / Stories sections list no design assets, and ADR-0235's own References gained its link in the same unseen commit. The session built two gauge-card dashboards before the owner said: "the session that did this mock previously forgot to provide you its assets hence why you build a dashboard for me and not what i wanted".
impact: Two full visualization rounds thrown away and an owner correction spent on re-steering rather than on the decision the session existed to take. The blast radius is any session that orients through an arc while a sibling session's asset is mid-flight: `arc show` is the prescribed orientation surface, so following the discipline exactly is what produced the miss. It also produced a reasoning error that reached a draft ADR — an argument that the owner's 500k threshold was off-scale, which was only falsified by the reference trace the session had not seen.
